item.content:encoded:
SCP-5295 is an anomalous fiction storybook that changes it's content every 5-7 days. When SCP-5295 is read by a human the first 3-5 chapters will seem normal compared to an average storybook but all chapters after chapter 5 have been recorded to become darker and more of a horror story. These chapters have been named the "Devil's chapters". When a human begins to read the Devil's chapters their mental state instantly starts to deteriorate. The more that is read, the quicker the deterioration.

Deleted at -14 and three votes.

/scp-5672 (no title) by Doctor Cheese deleted at -15 and three votes.

SCP-5672-A, SCP-5672-B and SCP-5672-C are the skeletons of humans, each being around 6'2" and weighing 27 pounds average. They were found in a cave in █████, England. They were found in a large pool of liquid, found to be a mix of water with several minerals in, and strange glue like green substance.

/scp-5129 (The Hiker) by Thogri deleted at -17 and three votes.

SCP-5129 is an entity that appears randomly in various parts of the Norwegian wilderness, thought to be its primary hunting grounds. It appears as a humanoid creature roughly 1,8 meters in height and wearing green and black winter clothing, it covers its head with the hood of its jacket and has never been observed without it. Due to SCP-5129 anomalous abilities the only known detail about its face is that it has a warm and friendly smile similar to that of a loved one.

/a-closer-examination-of-scp-173 (A Closer Examination of SCP-173) by Kothardarastrix deleted at -15 and three votes.

Of all the anomalous objects in Foundation custody, there is one that everyone knows. We all read its file when we were in training, and for those of us who trained at Site-19, it was our first up-close and personal encounter with the anomalous. I still remember the first time I saw it; the eye-watering stink of its containment chamber, the blank stare of its fading, sprayed-on face, and, most of all, the sudden understanding that the slightest mistake would send that statue hurtling across the room to wrap its concrete hands around my neck.

Feedback ported:

[+] from Ethagon
– hide block

I like the idea of both the paper itself, the use of cross-testing for actual research, and the "conclusion" it arrives at, but there are a few things that made me downvote:

  • the size of the letters (this is the least important one)
  • Analyzing the documentation of SCP-173. This only makes sense out-of-universe. In-universe it would make more sense to frame this as an analysis of SCP-173's properties itself.
  • I think the writing could still be written a bit more clinical. It also didn't flow very well.
  • The paper makes a hypothesis at multiple points and then proceeds as if the hypothesis was proven fact. It would help a lot if more experimentation was done to support the hypothesis before moving on.
  • It would be better if the two theories at the end, quantum state and extradimensional control, were more aligned with each other. If they were more connected, it would feel more like "everything adds up" instead of a retroactive explanation for SCP-173. The quantum state theory adds a lot to these, as it really "fits" SCP-173 in a way. The extradimensional control theory, not so much.
[+] from The Pighead
– hide block

OK, so for this one, here's short reasons for why I've downvoted.

First of all, I want to be clear that I don't think your article is bad by any means. You've clearly done work about that, the grammar is perfect and the way you write it is pretty good, I've not really seem something that looked non-clinical or something like that.

But there's two reasons of why I downvote. The first one is the fact that, when I've readed some paragraphs, I've thought at least two times "Wait a minute, that looks like a SCPDeclassified post who weirdly tries to take an in-universe approach" and it felt off-topic at times (Wizz talked about the fact that in the article, 173 is a famous thing and it feels weird).

And the second reason is that, even if it's clear that you've done work and research, the paragraphs and the way it's organized looks like big walls of text, to the point that I had struggle reading that because there was too much words and too much scientific things implied, I was a bit lost.

So, that's why I downvote. But I can see a great lot of potential on your Tale, so I highly suggest you to rework it and pay attention to what others suggested you to do.

[+] from Nagiros
– hide block

Frankly I'm unconvinced that we need more 173 content in 2020. I respect the article a fair bit but I'm hardly invested in the character enough for anything resembling this.

Additionally, really not a fan of how the text resizing overadjusts. It's far too large as is.

scp-5441 is a body of water like substance of an undetermined size, and an immeasurable depth, many samples of scp-5441 have been collected from inside the containment zone, all results so far have come back as negative to any foreign bodies present in the water, further research is required.

/scp-5212 (The House From Somewhere Else) by Sami Gibbons deleted at -16 after the author blanked the page. Yossipossi witnessed.

SCP-5212 is a late 20th-century house, in the small town of ██████, in Dallas Texas. The building is made of a brick outer wall covering most of the house and tall stone pillars holding up the veranda. The steps to the porch of the house are in disrepair, and the veranda above the porch is in the process of falling apart, with the wood rotting away. The door of the house is to be kept closed until an expedition is permitted.

item.content:encoded:
SCP-5138 appears as a small grove of Japanese White Birch (Betula Platyphylla) in [REDACTED], Scotland. The anomaly always appears in autumnal colours and sheds a seemingly infinite amount of otherwise non-anomalous leaves. Walking down the grove will lead to a bamboo archway, which, when entered transports individuals to a traditional Japanese garden, hereby referred to as SCP-5138-1. The garden has been reported to evoke feelings of peace in all cases.

Deleted at -22 and three votes. Rewrite by Ayumi-san is pending.

SCP-5358 is a human male about twenty-four (24) years in age, and standing about 1.8 meters in height. Medical checkups so far have found no physical anomalies on the internal and external body of SCP-5358. IQ tests have given it a slightly above-average intelligence level of 116.

Deleted at -18 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

Unihedron

+ show block
– hide block

I'm sorry to say, but this feels really incomplete. Whatever intrigue that the article brings me remains unanswered throughout to the end and quite honestly this feels like it's written by someone who doesn't understand or bothered attempting to elaborate on why being able to hack into outright anything is anomalous, or even interesting. The name drop to UIU had a reverse impact on me; instead of making me feel "wow, they could do that?" it made me go "there's no way this makes sense".

I think this suffers a case of show-don't-tell in that I'm being told how outrageous the situation is but nothing that pulls its weight and make it feel grand, rather that it's odd being delivered this way. I think the places in the article like the breach and the high cooperation level as shown could be translated into logs that are interesting to read and experience, but in its current form it really feels lacking.

FluffyDog00

+ show block
– hide block

In order for an article to work, there needs to be a strong narrative with a clear beginning, middle, and end. This has a beginning and a middle. There are no stakes, just a dude who is really good at something, and has no further character development other than that. It's boring and tasteless.

-1

SCP-5368-A is an entity that infused itself with Tiger tank 132, designated as SCP-5368-B. SCP-5368-A can utilize all of SCP-5368-B's system, including its 88 mm cannon and 2× 7.92 mm MG34. SCP-5368-A also apparently has some unique abilities and characteristics as the weapons and armor on SCP-5368-B seems to be enhanced, allowing better protection and firepower. SCP-5368 is remarkably aggressive and territorial. All non-personnel must not come in contact with it. If aggravated, SCP-5368 will become hostile and attempt to destroy anything in its vicinity. All SCP Foundation personnel guarding SCP-5368 must immediately respond and engage until SCP-5368 reverts back to its passive mode, which averagely lasts from 30 minutes to 2 hours. Air support is necessary as it will presumably bring the time of aggravation down by half an hour, but still remains harmless to SCP-5368. Any non-personnel who come into contact with SCP-5368 must be given amnestics and misinformed by MTF Gamma-5.

Deleted at -16 and three votes.

item.content:encoded:
/scp-5492 (no title) by CocoaIzBlu deleted at -20 and three votes.

SCP-5492 is a speaker-like object produced somewhere in the 1800s, probably tracing back to 1877. Object#: 5492 is a half-rotten spruce cuboid, plated with metal speakers made with aluminium. Its main colour is white due to the clear lack of pigmentation in SCP-5492's shape, making the wood hard to classify to the eye.

Feedback ported:

[+] from DoctorSasbo
– hide block

It's really unfortunate that everybody is downvoting this without actually commenting suggestions to help it. Here's my two cents:

The biggest issue with this imo is the prose:

  • "immensely scant amount of room, and heaps of soundproof foam" is not clinical enough for an official document. Try saying "an enclosed space insulated by soundproof foam", or state the measurements if you want to drive home the extent of it
  • "due to the lack of knowledge on SCP-5492" - If it's being researched, we already know there's a lack of knowledge, so the phrase is redundant
  • "somewhere in the 1800s, probably tracing back to 1877" - Firstly, I think you meant "sometime" instead of "somewhere." Secondly, if you have that specific of a year, it doesn't make sense to add uncertainty by saying "probably." Finally, you might want to briefly say where it's from/was found.
  • "Its main colour is white due to the clear lack of pigmentation in SCP-5492's shape, making the wood hard to classify to the eye" could just be "It is predominantly white." You're spending a lot of words elaborating on something that could be written more concisely.
  • "at the first glances… teeth to commit suicide." is too long of a sentence, try breaking it up into multiple sentences so the reader can more effectively process it
  • ""the noise is so dreadful it's better to die than live to remember the horror" - Which was said by a test subject." I get what you're going for, but it comes off as kinda flat and cliche. You might want to flesh it out a bit more with an interview log, so you can go more in detail about the effects on the subject.
  • "the unfathomable entity" doesn't fit the clinical tone. It's SCP-5492.
  • "When the surviving Subject made it out of the containment he was insane and instead of being suicidal he was critically homicidal instead." Instead of just saying he's homicidal, try describing what he did i.e. stab researchers, torture fellow D-class, etc.

Overall, I think this is a workable concept, but the execution is severely lacking. Tighten up your prose, and try to elaborate more on what actually happens so you can show instead of just telling. Hope this helps!

item.content:encoded:
All Staff-enacted Deletions are carried out according to the Deletions Guide.

Summary deletions result for:

  • Articles with malicious intent
  • Pages that are clearly unfinished.
  • Attempts to "game" site procedure, such as re-posting a non-rewritten article in an attempt to get around downvotes.
  • Blatantly plagiarized material.
  • An article posted outside of the current range.

If an author attempts to self-delete their work and fails to do so properly, including either by blanking the page or renaming it, it will be deleted properly by Staff.
